records.query: To verify acquired myopathy, core items are serum CK/aldolase, inflammatory markers, myositis antibody panel, thyroid/electrolytes, and needle EMG; current belief lacks all these, and no prior retrieval exists. Need serum CK and aldolase, needle EMG, and myositis antibody panel results (critical to confirm myopathy and exclude GBS/NMJ).

To verify acquired myopathy, core items are serum CK/aldolase, inflammatory markers, myositis antibody panel, thyroid/electrolytes, and needle EMG; current belief lacks all these, and no prior retrieval exists. Need serum CK and aldolase, needle EMG, and myositis antibody panel results (critical to confirm myopathy and exclude GBS/NMJ).

Need cerebrospinal fluid analysis (protein, cell count, albuminocytologic dissociation) and serum anti-ganglioside antibodies, plus repeat nerve conduction study with F-waves, to confirm or exclude Guillain-Barré syndrome after needle EMG showed neurogenic recruitment, which argues against acquired myopathy. Serum CK/aldolase and myositis antibody panel also remain essential to definitively rule out myopathy.

Need cerebrospinal fluid analysis (protein, cell count, albuminocytologic dissociation) and serum anti-ganglioside antibodies, plus repeat nerve conduction study with F-waves, to confirm or exclude Guillain-Barré syndrome after needle EMG showed neurogenic recruitment, which argues against acquired myopathy. Serum CK/aldolase and myositis antibody panel also remain essential to definitively rule out myopathy.

Need serum creatine kinase, needle electromyography, and cerebrospinal fluid protein plus serial nerve conduction studies. These are core to verify acquired myopathy (via myopathic EMG/CK changes) and exclude Guillain-Barré syndrome (via CSF protein and NCS evolution), given proximal weakness, tingling, hyporeflexia, and normal initial NCS.

Need serum creatine kinase, needle electromyography, and cerebrospinal fluid protein plus serial nerve conduction studies. These are core to verify acquired myopathy (via myopathic EMG/CK changes) and exclude Guillain-Barré syndrome (via CSF protein and NCS evolution), given proximal weakness, tingling, hyporeflexia, and normal initial NCS.

Need muscle biopsy with histochemistry/immunohistochemistry and serum aldolase level (core to confirm or exclude acquired myopathy, given neurogenic recruitment on needle EMG conflicts with myopathic pattern).

bindings.label: 49-year-old male had sudden onset of proximal muscle weakness in both upper and lower limbs accompanied by tingling and pain
49-year-old male was admitted in July 2010 due to sudden onset of weakness in the proximal muscles of his limbs, affecting both sensory and motor functions
Clinical examination showed proximal muscle weakness in both upper and lower limbs, tingling and pain, and reduced muscle stretch reflexes in the lower limbs
There were no signs of upper motor neuron involvement
Nerve conduction studies showed normal results
Needle EMG shows abnormal spontaneous activity and neurogenic recruitment
